items.title: Directive (EU) 2026/470 amending Directives 2006/43/EC, 2013/34/EU, (EU) 2022/2464 and (EU) 2024/1760 (the Omnibus I Directive)
items.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (Official Journal of the European Union)
items.locator: Article 2(4)(b), inserting new subparagraphs into Article 19a(3) of Directive 2013/34/EU (and Article 2(5) for the matching text in Article 29a(3)); Article 2(8), new Article 29ca; recital 12; Article 5(1); Article 6
items.quote: Protected undertakings shall have the right to decline to provide information exceeding the information specified in the voluntary standards
items.why: The binding rule and the source of the quotation. Defines a protected undertaking as one that does not exceed, on its balance sheet date, an average of 1 000 employees during the preceding financial year and is in the value chain of a reporting undertaking. Reporting undertakings must not require more than the voluntary standards; contrary contract terms are not binding; a request that goes further must say which information exceeds the standards and that the supplier has a statutory right to decline. The right covers only requests made for sustainability reporting under the directive, not due diligence or other purposes, and nothing obliges a supplier to provide anything. A directive: member states must transpose by 19 March 2027. Official Journal text served by the Publications Office. The page prints '1 000' with a non-breaking space.

items.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1560 establishing sustainability reporting standards for voluntary use by undertakings protected by the value chain cap
items.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (Official Journal of the European Union)
items.locator: Article 1, Article 3 and Article 4; recitals 4 to 6; Annex II 'List of disclosures covered by the value chain cap'
items.quote: The value chain cap shall only comprise the datapoints specified in Annex II to this Regulation.
items.why: Where the line is drawn in practice. The cap is not the whole voluntary standard but the datapoints listed in Annex II, with a shorter list for undertakings with 10 employees or less. Emissions targets, climate risks and Scope 3 emissions are not on the list. Article 3 applies from financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027. Recital 4 limits the cap to information gathered for reporting under Directive 2013/34/EU. Recital 5 only 'encourages' banks and insurers to keep other requests within the standard.

items.title: Commission Delegated Regulation C(2026) 5011 final: explanatory memorandum
items.locator: Explanatory memorandum, section 1 (PDF pages 2 to 3) and section 3 (PDF pages 5 to 6)
items.quote: protected undertakings have a statutory right to refuse to provide information exceeding those limits
items.why: The Commission's own explanation of how the directive and the regulation fit together, including that the value chain cap does not stop information being shared voluntarily and does not affect requests made under other law. The explanatory memorandum is not part of the text published in the Official Journal; use it to understand the rule, not as the rule. In this adopted version Article 3(1) reads 'not subject to mandatory reporting requirements'; the Official Journal text reads 'subject to'.

items.title: Commission Staff Working Document SWD(2026) 500 final, accompanying the two delegated regulations of 3 July 2026
items.locator: Passage on the value chain cap, PDF page 6 (printed page 5); section 4.1, PDF pages 19 to 20 (printed pages 18 to 19)
items.quote: Only essential disclosures are covered by the value chain cap
items.why: Explains the design choices: a single employee test so that customers can apply it easily; a gap for undertakings with more than 1 000 employees but turnover below EUR 450 million, which are neither reporting nor protected; and a lower cap for undertakings with 10 employees or fewer. Commission services' analysis, not law.

items.title: Implementing and delegated acts: Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive
items.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Financial Stability, Financial Services and Capital Markets Union
items.quote: for voluntary use by undertakings protected by the value chain cap (not in force until it is published in the Official Journal)
items.why: The Commission's index of the instruments, with links to the adopted texts, annexes and staff working document. Not yet updated: the page, last updated 3 July 2026, still describes the regulation as 'not in force until it is published in the Official Journal', although it was published as Regulation (EU) 2026/1560 on 21 September 2026.

items.title: Commission adopts revised sustainability reporting standards
items.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Financial Stability, Financial Services and Capital Markets Union
items.locator: News article, paragraph on the voluntary reporting standard
items.quote: companies subject to the CSRD cannot require companies in their value chains to provide more information than is covered by the voluntary standard
items.why: The plainest official statement of the cap, suitable for quoting to a customer. It is a summary: it does not mention that the cap is limited to the datapoints in Annex II or to requests made for the customer's own sustainability report.

items.title: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2025/1710 on a voluntary sustainability reporting standard for small and medium-sized undertakings
items.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (Official Journal of the European Union)
items.locator: Recitals 14 and 17; points 4 to 6 of the Recommendation
items.quote: large corporates and financial intermediaries should limit, as far as possible, such requests to information that is coherent with the disclosures included in the VSME
items.why: The position before the right existed: a request to large companies and lenders to show restraint, with no power for the supplier to refuse. Useful to show what changed. Recital 5 of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1560 says the Recommendation should be considered as no longer producing any legal effects from that regulation's entry into force. Official Journal text served by the Publications Office.

items.title: PPN 006: Taking account of Carbon Reduction Plans in the procurement of major government contracts
items.quote: provision of a CRP in accordance with this PPN must be relevant and proportionate to the contract
items.why: The nearest UK equivalent to a limit on what may be asked: government buyers are told that the demand for a Carbon Reduction Plan must be relevant and proportionate to the contract. It is policy guidance to buyers, binds central government only, and gives the supplier no statutory right to decline. No UK statute containing a right like the EU one was found in this pass.

items.title: Feedback on sustainability reporting standards: additional explanatory information regarding the value chain cap
items.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Financial Stability, Financial Services and Capital Markets Union
items.quote: It means only that they cannot require companies with 1000 employees or fewer to provide certain information.
items.why: The Commission's own questions and answers on how the right works in practice. A customer may still ask for more than the cap but cannot require it, must mark which items go beyond the cap and must tell the supplier of its statutory right to decline; applying the voluntary standard does not stop other requests; and customers are expected to ask for less than the cap where they do not need it all. Explanatory, not law, and written on 6 May 2026 about the draft standard then out for feedback: it describes the cap as the disclosures marked 'necessary', whereas the adopted regulation defines it by the list in Annex II. Follow the regulation where they differ.

items.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 as regards the simplification of certain sustainability reporting standards
items.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (Official Journal of the European Union)
items.locator: Annex, ESRS 1 General Requirements, chapter 5, paragraph 66; paragraph 65 on estimates; Article 3 (entry into force and application)
items.quote: This limitation also applies to non-EU undertakings in the upstream and downstream value chain of the reporting undertaking.
items.why: The customer's side of the line, and the passage that matters most to a UK supplier. The reporting standard binding on EU companies in scope tells them that what may be required from protected undertakings comprises only the Annex II datapoints, and that this limit also applies to non-EU undertakings in their value chain. Paragraph 65 lets the customer use estimates instead of supplier data, so a refusal does not leave the customer unable to report. A rule addressed to the reporting customer, not a right enforceable by a UK firm in a UK court; that question was not researched. Enters into force on 10 November 2026 and applies to financial years from 1 January 2027. Official Journal text served by the Publications Office.

items.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2464 as regards corporate sustainability reporting (the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive), as originally published
items.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (Official Journal of the European Union)
items.locator: Article 1(8), inserting Article 29b into Directive 2013/34/EU, paragraph 4
items.quote: Sustainability reporting standards shall specify disclosures on value chains that are proportionate and relevant to the capacities and the characteristics of undertakings in value chains
items.why: Where the line came from. The 2022 directive already said that reporting standards must not require companies to obtain from small and medium-sized undertakings in their value chain more than the standard for listed small companies. That was a limit on the standard-setter, not a right the supplier could use, and the 2026 directive records that disproportionate requests continued notwithstanding it. Explains why a refusal position written before 2026 has no statutory basis. This is the text as published on 16 December 2022; Directive (EU) 2026/470 has since amended these provisions, so do not cite it as current law.

items.title: Procurement Act 2023, section 12: Covered procurement: objectives
items.locator: s.12(4); see also s.22(1) and (5) on proportionate conditions of participation
items.quote: have regard to the fact that small and medium-sized enterprises may face particular barriers to participation
items.why: The nearest UK statutory basis for pushing back, and it applies to public buyers only. A contracting authority must have regard to the barriers small and medium-sized enterprises face and consider whether they can be removed or reduced, and under section 22 may set conditions of participation only if they are a proportionate means of ensuring capacity or ability to perform. A supplier facing an excessive sustainability questionnaire in a public tender can cite these duties. They are duties on the buyer, not a right to decline, and say nothing about private customers. The page shows no known outstanding effects and a current version dated 24 February 2025.

items.title: UK SRS S1: General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information
items.locator: Appendix B, paragraphs B6 and B8 to B10 (printed pages 23 to 24, PDF pages 27 to 28)
items.quote: An entity need not undertake an exhaustive search for information to identify sustainability-related risks and opportunities
items.why: What a UK reporting customer is actually obliged to gather. The UK standard asks it to use reasonable and supportable information available without undue cost or effort, and says an exhaustive search is not needed. A supplier can point to this when a UK customer claims its own reporting compels a demand: the standard does not require the customer to obtain everything. It gives the supplier no right to decline and is voluntary unless another rule, such as the listing rules, applies it.

items.title: Scope 3 Emissions in the UK Reporting Landscape: Call for Evidence Analysis Report
items.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
items.locator: Chapter 1, 'Compliance with IFRS', PDF page 14; chapter 2, 'Data challenges', item 6, PDF page 20
items.quote: a set of overarching principles that prioritise proportionality, and materiality, will help to balance the requests on SMEs for data inputs
items.why: Shows the UK has recognised the problem without legislating on it. Respondents to the government's call for evidence asked for proportionality principles to limit requests to small firms and raised confidentiality of supplier information as a concern. Supports the brief's finding that no UK equivalent of the EU right exists. Dated May 2024. An analysis of 184 self-selected responses; views of respondents, not government policy.

items.title: Data Requests in Value Chains: The Effects of Corporate Sustainability Reporting on SMEs in The Netherlands
items.publisher: Niemann, Morssinkhof, van der Linden and de Vries, Sustainability 17(17), 8029 (MDPI); copy held in the Delft University of Technology repository
items.locator: Section 1, Introduction (article page 2, PDF page 3); end of section 3.2 (article page 8, PDF page 9)
items.quote: business partners can in principle impose contractual demands for data that they consider material
items.why: Peer-reviewed evidence of the pressure the right is meant to answer. The authors note that a voluntary standard alone does not protect a small firm, because customers can write data demands into contracts, and report that the burden grows when different customers ask for different data on the same product. Written before Directive (EU) 2026/470 made contract terms that go beyond the standard non-binding for reporting purposes, so it describes the position the directive changed. Survey of 431 Dutch firms and 48 interviews, late 2024. Read in the university repository's copy of the final published version.

items.title: Supply-chain data sharing for scope 3 emissions
items.publisher: Stenzel and Waichman, npj Climate Action 2, article 7 (Springer Nature)
items.locator: Section 'Obstacles to primary data sharing', paragraphs on data privacy concerns
items.quote: Firms are very hesitant to share such data.
items.why: Peer-reviewed review of why suppliers hold back emissions data, and a legitimate ground for refusal that is separate from the EU right: product-level emissions data can reveal production processes, product composition and supplier networks, so it is competitively sensitive. Supports a refusal position that distinguishes aggregate figures from commercially sensitive detail. A review article, not new empirical work; it concerns emissions data only and predates the 2026 rules. Open access on the publisher's site.
